blocking_findings: F1 [Major] ux-browser-review: the 60-character week title overflows the title plaque at 568x320 in English and in Thai. Measured in the app (J1, real route /en/st/3/6 and /th/st/3/6, the Thai string of adversarial case V1): plaque_overflow_px=20, overflow_top_px=20, overflow_bottom_px=0, clipped_text=0, title_chars=60, plaque_h_px=40, for en and for th. The same row at 320x568 reads plaque_overflow_px=0, clipped_text=0, plaque_h_px=272. The cause is the landscape rule of apps/storytime/app/look.css lines 821-831: inside @media (max-height: 500px) the rule header[data-hero] > h1 sets height: 40px and min-height: 40px, so the fixed plaque box cannot hold a wrapped 60-character title and the text leaves the box upward. The PNGs are measure/runs/storytime_look_20261107/ux-p2-c54b78ea4/council-r4/extra/plaque-en-568x320.png and measure/runs/storytime_look_20261107/ux-p2-c54b78ea4/council-r4/extra/plaque-th-568x320.png; in both the title text sits above the blue plaque and over the hero bar. Rationale: test-strategy.md P2.4 row 3 (line 587) requires that a 60-character title cause no overflow and no clipped text, and P2.6 line 613 names 568x320 as an adversarial viewport; the canonical gate row 3 measures the long title only at 390x844, so no canonical row fails on this, and the adversarial r2 record routed this exact browser measurement to the UX browser review. The longest shipped title of content/l2 is 13 characters ('Unit 1 Review' and 'Is It a Ball?'), and a J3 check with the real app/look.css reads plaque_overflow_px=0 for that title at 568x320, so the defect is latent for the shipped content and real for the 60-character title that row 3 names. Exit criterion: plaque_overflow_px=0 for the 60-character English and Thai title at 568x320, with the other rows of the gate unchanged. Owner: Green.
nonblocking_findings: F2 [Minor] ux-browser-review: at the 200 percent page zoom of a 390 CSS px phone the layout viewport is 195 CSS px, below the 320 CSS px reflow floor of WCAG 1.4.10, so the horizontal overflow of that case is a note and not a defect. Measured (J1): page_overflow=104 (week), 72 (reader), 37 (song), 37 (decodable) at a 195x422 CSS px viewport, with clipped_text=0 on all four screens. Owner: none for this phase.

F3 [Minor] ux-browser-review: the app pins its type in px, so a browser text-size setting does not enlarge the look text. Measured (J1): the root font size at 32px (both the root font size rule and the CDP default font size command) leaves sentence_px=25 and plaque_px=28 or 36 unchanged, and every screen reads page_overflow=0 and clipped_text=0 under both. The two font-size emulations therefore measure nothing about the look type, and the page zoom of F2 is the only zoom case that scales it. Owner: none for this phase; record the finding for the look check of Daniel on 2026-11-18.

F4 [Nit] ux-browser-review: two defects of my own harness were found and corrected during J1, and both change a measured value. First, the first plaque metric read scrollHeight minus clientHeight of the plaque; it read 0 overflow at 568x320 while the PNG showed the Thai title leaving the plaque box, because the landscape rule fixes the plaque height at 40 px, so scrollHeight never passes clientHeight. The metric now measures the text box of a Range over the title against the box of the plaque, and it reads overflow_top_px=20. Second, the first two zoom emulations set the root font size and the browser default font size, and both left the type of the app unscaled because app/look.css sets every font size in px; those runs measured nothing, and the third emulation, the page zoom of 200 percent, is the one that scales the px type and produces the overflow of F2. Owner: none; this is the evidence record of the review.

F1 cause in the shipped source: apps/storytime/app/look.css lines 821-831 hold the landscape rule header[data-hero] > h1 with height: 40px and min-height: 40px inside @media (max-height: 500px), against the base rule of lines 209-235 that uses width: fit-content, max-width: calc(100% - 24px) and min-height: 88px with no nowrap.

F1 scope in the shipped content: the longest title of content/l2 is 13 characters ('Unit 1 Review' in w08 and 'Is It a Ball?' in w07), and a J3 check that loads the real app/look.css over a copy of the markup of frame.tsx reads plaque_overflow_px=0 for that title at 320x568 and at 568x320, against 9 for the 60-character seed at 568x320. The landscape rule also governs 844x390, a study viewport, and the canonical gate row 3 measures the long title only at 390x844.
F2 measurement (J1, page zoom of 200 percent, a 195x422 CSS px viewport): page_overflow=104 (week), 72 (reader), 37 (song), 37 (decodable), clipped_text=0 on all four screens.

F3 measurement (J1): the root font size at 32px leaves sentence_px=25 and plaque_px=28 or 36 unchanged on every screen, and page_overflow=0 and clipped_text=0 everywhere; the CDP default font size command reads the same root_px=32px with the same unchanged sizes.

Forced colors (J1, the routed adversarial gap): forced_media=true on both screens; the decodable sound button stays visible with pressed_label='Playing' and the done badge stays visible with badge_stroke=rgb(0, 0, 0) and badge_stroke_width=3.4px.

The two 568x320 plaque captures show the 60-character title rendered above the blue plaque over the hero bar, which matches overflow_top_px=20.
